title: Supercubic uniform formula lower bounds for SAT
formal: Does there exist a constant \(\varepsilon >0\) such that no LOGTIME-uniform De Morgan formula family computing \(\mathrm{SAT}_{n}\) for every n has \(O(n^{3+\varepsilon})\) leaves?
why: Would cross the cubic exponent for uniform De Morgan formula lower bounds on SAT. This quantifies a limitation of tree-shaped Boolean computation on an NP-complete problem without demanding a full separation from every polynomial-size family.
status_note: Source statement, model and the cited subsequent or baseline result checked; subsequent-work searches through 11 September 2026 located no resolution of this exact uniform SAT size question. No exhaustive literature or independent proof audit is claimed.

progress.text: Williams states the supercubic uniform SAT formula question and records the nearly cubic lower-bound baseline.

Bathie and Williams prove a larger-than-\(3 \log _{2} n\) depth lower bound for uniform NAND circuits solving SAT. Their paper explicitly distinguishes circuit depth, gate basis and formula-size lower bounds.

sentences: A De Morgan formula computes with binary AND and OR gates and input negations, without sharing internal computations.
Its size counts leaf occurrences, and the target function is SAT on n bits encoding a 3-CNF formula.
The source asks whether a fixed positive exponent can raise the required size beyond the cubic scale when the formula family is LOGTIME-uniform.
Later NAND depth lower bounds use a different gate basis and cost measure, so they do not directly settle this question.
The problem seeks a concrete improvement in uniform formula lower bounds for a central NP-complete language.

upgraded_from.title: Supercubic uniform formula lower bounds for SAT

definitions: The input is an explicitly encoded 3-CNF formula, as permitted by the source’s SAT convention. To fix a binary representation, encode a literal by a sign bit (0 for \(x_{i}\), 1 for \(\neg x_{i}\)), followed by the positive index i in Elias gamma code: \(\lfloor \log _{2}i\rfloor\) zero bits followed by the ordinary binary representation of i. Consecutive triples of literals are clauses, and the formula is their conjunction. Repeated literals and clauses are allowed, the empty conjunction is true, and malformed strings are rejected. \(\mathrm{SAT}_{n}:\{0,1\}^{n}\to \{0,1\}\) is 1 exactly for strings encoding satisfiable formulas. The parameter n counts all encoding bits, including signs and indices, rather than the number of distinct variables or clauses. This explicit binary-list convention fixes the source’s otherwise implicit SAT representation. A De Morgan formula is a rooted tree with AND and OR gates of fan-in two. Each leaf is an input bit, its negation, or a Boolean constant. Equivalently, unary NOT gates can be used anywhere and then pushed to the leaves without changing the leaf count. Internal computations cannot be shared between two parents. Its size is the number of leaf occurrences, so repeated uses of the same variable are charged separately. All input strings must be answered exactly. A family is LOGTIME-uniform when one deterministic machine, given binary n and a binary position j, returns the requested bit of the description of its n-input formula or circuit in \(O(\log  n)\) time, on a standard multitape Turing machine; positions outside the description return zero. Descriptions are explicit binary netlists: a header gives the number of nodes and the output node, nodes have consecutive binary identifiers and gate-type records, and a list gives each wire’s source, destination and input port, with negation flags when applicable. Each integer field is self-delimited in binary. Input-node records give their input-bit indices or a constant 0 or 1. The family may choose a consistent numbering but must have one such uniform description algorithm for every n. There is no advice and no randomness. Polynomial-size candidate families have polynomial-length descriptions and \(O(\log  n)\)-bit identifiers; the machine’s description and running-time constant are independent of n. The exponent \(\varepsilon\) is chosen once, before quantifying over families and their uniformity machines. A family has \(O(n^{3+\varepsilon})\) leaves if some constant C bounds its size by \(Cn^{3+\varepsilon}\) for all sufficiently large n. Constants may depend on the family and \(\varepsilon\), but not n. The source writes “requires” such size; the formal statement adopts uniform-class nonmembership, equivalently arbitrarily large failures of each candidate big-O bound.
answer_criterion: Prove that there is a fixed \(\varepsilon >0\) for which every correct LOGTIME-uniform De Morgan formula family has, for every \(C>0\) and every \(N_{0}\), some \(n\ge N_{0}\) with more than \(Cn^{3+\varepsilon}\) leaves. Alternatively, refute this by proving that for every \(\varepsilon >0\) some correct LOGTIME-uniform family has \(O(n^{3+\varepsilon})\) leaves. The target is exact worst-case computation of SAT, with the stated basis, uniformity and size measure.

context_blocks.title: A quantitative lower bound for satisfiability
context_blocks.text: The object computing SAT receives the bits of a formula and outputs whether some assignment satisfies it. This card asks whether even a uniformly described De Morgan formula must exceed the \(n^{3}\) scale by a fixed positive exponent. The circuit or formula that decides SAT is distinct from the 3-CNF formula encoded in its input.

context_blocks.title: What is being counted
context_blocks.text: The formula \((a\land b)\lor (a\land c)\) has four leaf occurrences, although it mentions only three variables. This illustrates why a formula-size bound counts uses of inputs, not distinct variable names. The benchmark size is for the formula computing SAT on n encoding bits.

context_blocks.title: Uniformity constrains the whole family
context_blocks.text: A separate small circuit for every input length could contain information chosen independently at each length. LOGTIME-uniformity requires one short-running algorithm to describe all those circuits locally. The input to that description algorithm is the input length and a position in the description, not a particular SAT instance.

context_blocks.title: A fixed exponent, with a stated asymptotic convention
context_blocks.text: The question is whether SAT lies outside the uniform size-\(O(n^{3+\varepsilon})\) class for some fixed \(\varepsilon >0\). Thus every correct uniform family must exceed any constant multiple of that bound at arbitrarily large lengths. This uses the standard class-nonmembership interpretation of the source’s lower-bound question; it does not add an almost-everywhere requirement.

context_blocks.title: Dated progress and its scope
context_blocks.text: The 2016 column records nearly cubic De Morgan formula lower bounds for SAT. Bathie and Williams’s ITCS 2024 paper obtains a depth lower bound of \(3.603 \log _{2} n\) for polylogtime-uniform NAND circuits solving SAT. NAND depth uses a restricted gate basis and a different cost measure; this statement alone does not settle the requested De Morgan leaf-size bound.
